title: Supervised Learning
subject: Machine Learning
content: Supervised learning is a type of machine learning where a model learns from labelled examples. Each training example contains input data and the correct answer. The model learns the relationship and then predicts answers for new data. Examples include spam detection and house-price prediction.
keywords: labelled data classification regression training prediction

title: Unsupervised Learning
subject: Machine Learning
content: Unsupervised learning finds patterns in data that has no labelled answers. The algorithm groups similar items or discovers structure. Clustering customers into groups is a common example. K-means is a popular clustering algorithm.
keywords: unlabelled data clustering grouping patterns k-means

title: Decision Tree
subject: Machine Learning
content: A decision tree is a model that makes a prediction by asking a sequence of questions. Each internal node is a question, each branch is an answer, and each leaf is a final prediction. It is easy to explain but can overfit if it grows too deep.
keywords: classification regression splits nodes leaves rules

title: Linear Regression
subject: Machine Learning
content: Linear regression predicts a numerical value by fitting a straight-line relationship between input features and an output. A simple model is y = mx + c, where m is the slope and c is the intercept. It is often used for trend and price prediction.
keywords: continuous value prediction line slope intercept

title: Overfitting
subject: Machine Learning
content: Overfitting happens when a model learns the training examples too closely, including noise. It performs very well on training data but poorly on new data. It can be reduced using more data, simpler models, regularization, or cross-validation.
keywords: generalization training testing regularization bias variance

title: Python Lists
subject: Programming
content: A Python list is an ordered and changeable collection. It can store multiple values in one variable. Lists use square brackets, for example numbers = [10, 20, 30]. You can access an item by its index, and the first index is zero.
keywords: python collection array append index mutable

title: Python Functions
subject: Programming
content: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a task. In Python, define a function with def, give it a name, and place the code inside an indented block. Functions can accept inputs called parameters and can return a result.
keywords: python def parameters return reusable code

title: Neural Networks
subject: Artificial Intelligence
content: A neural network is a machine-learning model inspired loosely by connected neurons. It contains layers of units that transform input values. During training, the model adjusts weights to reduce prediction error. Neural networks are used in image, speech, and language tasks.
keywords: deep learning layers weights activation training

title: Model Evaluation
subject: Machine Learning
content: Model evaluation measures how well a machine-learning model performs on data it has not seen during training. Common classification measures include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. A separate test set helps estimate performance on new examples.
keywords: accuracy precision recall f1 score test data
